name: AI diagnostics and clinical copilots
summary: AI assists clinicians with medical images, documentation, chart review and selected decision-support tasks.
useCase: A clinician reviews an automatically drafted visit note and an imaging alert, checks the underlying evidence, then signs the clinical record.
whyNow: AMA surveys show rapidly rising professional AI use, while the FDA’s device list demonstrates a growing regulated product base. Adoption is much broader than autonomous diagnosis: administrative assistance and summarisation contribute heavily to survey use.

mainstream.scope: Clinician-reviewed documentation and validated decision support in well-resourced health systems; specific approved diagnostic workflows.
mainstream.rationale: The labour-saving use case is immediate and survey adoption is already high. Moving from any experimentation to reliable integrated care requires local validation, outcome monitoring and workflow accountability. Autonomous clinical care is outside this forecast.

metric.name: Physicians reporting professional AI use in AMA surveys
metric.scope: US physician survey; any professional AI use, not autonomous diagnosis
metric.limitations: Different survey waves and respondent samples; the latest value is reported in a March 2026 release. Use includes research, notes and other assistance. Show percentage-point change, not CAGR or population-wide penetration.
metric.futureNote: No defensible like-for-like external forecast is available for this KPI. The forward maturity path is a separately labelled analyst scenario, not a numerical adoption forecast.
metric.growthLabel: +43 percentage points from 2023 to the 2026 survey release; respondent samples differ.

milestones.text: No comparable 2021 AMA AI-use survey point is included.
No comparable 2022 AMA AI-use survey point is included.
The first AMA comparison wave found 38% professional AI use.
The next survey found 66% professional AI use; this includes administrative and informational tasks.
AMA published the 2024 survey results, documenting growing physician use and interest.
AMA reported 81% use in its March 2026 release; FDA’s AI-enabled-device list continued to be updated.

tailwinds: Documentation burden gives a concrete return-on-time use case
Integration with existing records reduces workflow switching
Validated narrow tools can be deployed without solving all of medicine
bottlenecks: Hallucinated notes, biased performance and missed findings
Clinical evidence may not transfer between patient populations
Billing, consent, liability and monitoring require local implementation
watchMetrics: Time saved after clinician correction, not raw drafting speed
Prospective patient outcomes and error rates by subgroup
Active paid users and renewal rates versus free pilots

forwardInterpretation: The maturity path is an analyst scenario for the stated market scope. A score of 4 means routine use in that scope, not a measured adoption percentage. The window can shift if the listed cost, performance, evidence or policy bottlenecks fail to clear.
